newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI Victoria to buy small, medium firms.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI Victoria to buy small, medium firms.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund (NFI) No 5, or Victoria, which is part of the country's mass privatisation program wants to invest in small and medium non- public companies, the president of the fund said on Tuesday.
"Our strategy is based on investing in small and medium non-public companies. We want to increase their value and then sell," Jerzy Drygalski told Reuters in an interview.

He said the fund wanted to concentrate on increasing the value of companies such as chemical firm Erg SA, or textile firm Haft SA, and sell weaker ones. He also said the fund was planning to merge companies in its portfolio.
"We plan to merge our firms. The most advanced is a merger between Haft and carpet maker Weltom SA, the decision might be taken in the next few weeks," he said.

Drygalski also said that, in the next two years, the fund would place two or three of its companies on the bourse. He said it also wanted to sell by the end of 1997 the 33 percent stakes it holds in three or four companies that are part of its portfolio.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-size companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the program have been able to exchange them for 15 shares -- one in each fund. The shares will start trade on the Warsaw bourse on Thursday.
The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
